/about.html.title: About — Al-Haq Initiative | Founder & Mission
/about.html.content: About the Al-Haq Initiative The Al-Haq Initiative is dedicated to seeking truth in history and protecting health in the present. Our work fuses rigorous primary-source research with digital tools that empower the community. Our Mission At Al-Haq Studio, we believe in using technology to make a positive impact. That is why all of our free tools and community solutions are offered directly through the Al-Haq Initiative—our dedicated mission to provide free, high-quality digital tools to the public, entirely built and backed by our studio. We develop innovative, spiritually enriching digital solutions and historical research that help the community deepen knowledge, strengthen practice, and build resilience. Our Vision To be a trusted source of verified historical knowledge and protection tools, making authentic research and community-centered technology accessible to all. Our Values check_circle Truth in Sources: Rigorous verification through primary documents, never political distortion. check_circle Community Empowerment: Tools and resources that strengthen identity, scholarship, and wellbeing. check_circle Islamic Ethics: All content and technology reflects Islamic values and protects against harm. check_circle Free & Accessible: All research and core resources available free, no paywalls. About the Founder & Operational Structure Al-Haq Studio and the Al-Haq Initiative were founded by, and are wholly owned and operated by, Habibur Rahman Meranai as a UK sole trader. Al-Haq Studio functions as the commercial software development studio, while the Al-Haq Initiative functions as the non-profit digital welfare and historical research wing, with all software, research platforms, and infrastructure engineered and maintained by Habibur Rahman Meranai through Al-Haq Studio. • Software, products & services are engineered and delivered under Al-Haq Studio, his commercial sole-trader business. • Academic & literary works, including historical research, verified booklets, and translations, are authored personally by Habibur Rahman Meranai. The Al-Haq Initiative is not a registered charity or separate corporate entity; it operates as the digital welfare and community research wing of Al-Haq Studio.

/all-infographics.html.title: Infographics
/all-infographics.html.content: Unveiling the Western World Infographics An interactive exploration of the complex realities behind the facade of Western prosperity, based on the analysis from "Unveiling the Western World". The Foundation: A Colonial Legacy The book argues that modern Western wealth wasn't accidental, but built on a historical foundation of colonialism. This section explores the systematic process of exploitation that transferred resources from colonized lands to imperial centers, creating lasting global disparities. 1. Economic Hunger The industrial revolution created an insatiable demand for raw materials and new markets, driving the push for overseas expansion and resource extraction. 2. Invasion & Subjugation Military conquest, like the British invasions of Afghanistan, was used to subjugate local populations and ensure economic dependence. 3. Systematic Resource Theft Resources were plundered, often with brutal forced labor, such as in the Belgian Congo's rubber trade. This stolen wealth flowed to imperial centers. 4. The Enduring Legacy This history of imposed rule and extraction created the economic disparities and political instabilities that many formerly colonized nations still face. The Reality Within: Social Cracks Beyond the gleaming surface, the book highlights significant internal crises. This dashboard visualizes data on violent crime, public health, financial hardship, and personal safety, revealing a reality far from the idealized image. Disproportionate Violence The U.S. homicide rate is an outlier among developed nations. Pervasive Health Crises Data from the US & UK reveals deep-seated health challenges. Widespread Financial Hardship 27.1% of US adults faced food insecurity in 2024. 91% increase in rough sleeping in England over 3 years (to 2025). Pervasive Harassment 71% of all UK women have experienced sexual harassment in public. 86% This rises to 86% for young women aged 18-24. Source: UN Women UK The Global Impact: Intervention & Culture The book argues that Western influence extends globally through both overt foreign policy and pervasive cultural exports. Explore the case studies and concepts that illustrate this two-pronged impact. Foreign Intervention Cultural Imprint 1953: Iranian Coup The US and UK orchestrated the overthrow of democratically elected PM Mossadegh after he nationalized Iran's oil industry, installing a monarch friendly to Western interests. 1980s: Structural Adjustment The IMF & World Bank imposed programs on developing nations, forcing cuts to public services to service debts, often leading to mass protests and social unrest. 2003: Iraq Invasion Led by the US and UK on a false pretext, the invasion led to state collapse, immense loss of life, and regional destabilization, including the rise of ISIS. Consumerism A culture equating happiness with acquisition, fueling unsustainable consumption and personal debt. Individualism Prioritizing self-reliance over community, which can lead to social isolation and weakened support networks. The Media Machine Global media projects a curated, idealized image of the West, obscuring internal problems and historical injustices. A New Perspective The book concludes that a balanced understanding of the Western world requires moving beyond superficial perceptions. It calls for acknowledging the historical injustices that underpin its prosperity, recognizing its deep-seated internal challenges, and critically evaluating the global impact of its foreign policy and cultural dominance. For Eastern nations, this understanding offers liberation from the pressure to emulate a flawed model, empowering them to pursue authentic development paths. For the West, it is an urgent call for introspection and accountability. Ultimately, the goal is a shared future based on mutual respect, genuine collaboration, and a clear-eyed understanding of our interconnected world. Visit Golden Speech — Our Poems Collection All future poems will be hosted in the Golden Speech page.

/golden-speech.html.title: Golden Speech — Shifting Beliefs (Poem)
/golden-speech.html.content: Golden Speech Shifting Beliefs — A Poetic Journey A poetic reflection on faith, history, and the clarity of divine revelation. By Al-Haq Initiative. Shifting Beliefs Poetic Reflections on Faith Preface Faith shapes humanity, yet contradictions linger. This poetic journey traces Christianity’s historical struggles, Islam’s clarity, and the contrast between man‑made doctrine and divine revelation. Written in verse for the heart and the mind, it invites reflection more than debate. The First Light In lands of olive, sun, and stone, A man walked humbly, not alone. He spoke of One, the God above, Of mercy, guidance, truth, and love. No throne he claimed, no crown he bore, A prophet sent to hearts once sore. His words were light, his path was clear, A call to faith, not rule or fear. The faithful few, with hearts sincere, Kept holy law and held God near. No tangled creed, no three‑in‑one, Their worship simple, pure, undone. Yet distant lands and minds of lore Brought tales of more, of myths, and more. A mortal man made God on high, And from that spark, confusion nigh. Shaping Shadows The councils met in halls of stone, Where bishops sat, yet doubts had grown. They spoke of God, of man, of Son, And sought a creed that all could run. Debates were long, the voices high, No mortal mind could grasp the sky. Three persons said to form one Lord, A paradox in holy word. A man made God? Or God made man? The question shook the faithful clan. The scriptures strained to bear the claim, Yet still the doctrine found its name. And so arose a tangled thread, Where truth and myth together wed. The faithful followed, some unsure, Through shifting sands, no firm allure. Fading Scrolls The sacred texts in hands of men, Were copied, changed, again, again. From scroll to codex, line by line, Some truths endured, some lost in time. The gospels differ, tales collide, Genealogies shift, claims divide. Verses appear, then disappear, A scripture woven with human fear. Yet still they read, they kneel, they pray, Though doubts arise with each display. Blind faith persists, though questions grow, The seeds of confusion start to show. And in this haze of human hand, The creed of three began to stand. A mortal God, a man divine, A tangled faith, a shaky sign. The Steady Flame From desert sands a voice was heard, A truth revealed in every word. No tangled creed, no three‑in‑one, A single God, the only One. The Quran came, a guiding light, Unchanged by time, serene and bright. Each verse a drop, an ocean deep, A treasure hearts and souls can keep. Its message clear, its path divine, No paradox, no fractured line. Tawheed declared, the One, the Pure, A steadfast faith that shall endure. While others wrestle, lost, confused, With doctrines formed, then misused, The soul finds peace in God alone, A faith intact, a truth well known. Shifting Sand A God they claim is Three‑in‑One, A creed from which no sense is spun. Their proofs are built on shifting ground, A claim that reason can’t expound. They say a man of flesh and bone Is God eternal on His throne. A mortal man, a timeless Lord— A truth that breaks its own accord. The councils argued, sought to bind The thoughts that troubled every mind. But words like threads began to fray And pull belief in disarray. From fading script and human hand, A doctrine built on fragile land. With verses strained to bear the weight, They fortify a broken gate. In contrast stands the final Word, A peaceful truth, divinely heard. A steady flame untouched by doubt, The soul holds fast, belief devout. The final holy verse is read, And peace within the heart is spread. An ocean held in drops of ink, That shifts the way we live and think. Back to Infographics

/legal/alhaq-hub_docs/alhaq-hub_privacy_.title: Al-Haq Hub · Privacy Policy | Al-Haq Initiative
/legal/alhaq-hub_docs/alhaq-hub_privacy_.content: Back to Legal & Documentation Hub Al-Haq Hub · Privacy Policy Effective Date: 14 September 2025 · Last Updated: 2026 Legal & Operational Attribution Al-Haq Studio and the Al-Haq Initiative were founded by, and are wholly owned and operated by, Habibur Rahman Meranai as a UK sole trader. Al-Haq Studio functions as the commercial software development studio, while the Al-Haq Initiative functions as the non-profit digital welfare and historical research wing, with all software, research platforms, and infrastructure engineered and maintained by Habibur Rahman Meranai through Al-Haq Studio. Overview Al-Haq Hub is a digital productivity suite developed by Al-Haq Studio for the Al-Haq Initiative to provide faith-aligned daily utilities in a clean, distraction-free environment. We design all features to function locally on your device whenever possible. This policy explains what information we process, why we process it, and your controls. Scope This policy applies to Al-Haq Hub pages hosted by the Al-Haq Initiative and to Al-Haq Hub application clients (including Android and web platforms) referencing this document. It does not cover third-party websites or services that may link to or integrate with our tools. Information We Process Al-Haq Hub adheres to a strict local-by-default, data-minimisation architecture. Depending on feature usage, the application processes: Application Preferences: Theme selection, language choices, notification settings, and calculation methods, stored strictly on-device. Prayer & Qibla Inputs: Approximate or precise device coordinates (when permission is granted) and system time zone to compute solar angles and compass bearings locally. Voluntary Feedback: Comments and correspondence email addresses you explicitly provide when submitting inquiries or beta feedback. Local Diagnostic Data: Ephemeral system logs generated locally when debugging reported issues, never transmitted automatically. We do not sell personal data, we do not track browsing history, and we do not build advertising profiles. Device Permissions (Android Application) Location: Used exclusively to compute astronomical prayer times and Qibla direction on-device. You can revoke this permission at any time in system settings; the application will fall back to manual city selection. Notifications: Used to trigger local prayer alerts and opt-in reminders. Controlled directly through app settings and OS notification channels. Compass & Orientation: Used strictly during active Qibla compass viewing to calibrate direction. How We Use Information Deliver core utility functions (astronomical calculations, Qibla compass, local reminders) and personalise UI settings. Respond directly to user-initiated support requests and bug reports. Maintain platform integrity and comply with statutory obligations under UK law. On-Device Processing & Storage All mathematical calculations, astronomical algorithms, and prayer calendars execute directly on your local device hardware. Clearing your application storage or browser cache removes all locally saved preferences and history immediately. Cookies & Local Storage (Web) Our static web pages use only first-party local storage to remember your preferred language, dark mode theme, and reading progress. We do not deploy third-party advertising cookies, fingerprinting scripts, or cross-site trackers. Your Rights & Controls In compliance with the UK Data Protection Act 2018 and UK GDPR, you maintain complete rights to: Access, rectify, or request deletion of any correspondence data held in our support records. Revoke device permissions (Location, Notifications, Sensors) at any time. Export or purge all local application data directly through application settings. Contact the Data Controller For any questions regarding privacy, data rights, or technical practices, contact Habibur Rahman Meranai (Data Controller) at: Privacy Enquiries: privacy@alhaq-initiative.org Legal Operations: legal@alhaq.uk General Support: support@alhaq-initiative.org Back to Legal & Docs Hub View Terms of Service →

/legal/privacy_hub.html.content: Back to Legal & Documentation Hub Privacy Hub & Data Commitments Comprehensive privacy standards, zero-telemetry architecture, and local-first data principles governing all software engineered by Al-Haq Studio and distributed via the Al-Haq Initiative. Legal & Operational Disclosure Al-Haq Studio and the Al-Haq Initiative were founded by, and are wholly owned and operated by, Habibur Rahman Meranai as a UK sole trader. Al-Haq Studio functions as the commercial software development studio, while the Al-Haq Initiative functions as the non-profit digital welfare and historical research wing, with all software, research platforms, and infrastructure engineered and maintained by Habibur Rahman Meranai through Al-Haq Studio. Core Privacy Architecture Zero-Telemetry & No Tracking We do not include third-party advertising SDKs, tracking pixels, behavioral analytics, or session recording scripts in our applications. User activity is never monetised, profiled, or sold to third parties. 100% Tracking-Free On-Device AI Inference Visual content filtering (AmniHaze via LiteRT and TensorFlow Lite) processes all video streams and images directly on your local hardware. Zero screen frames, pixels, or images are transmitted across the network or saved remotely. On-Device Neural Models Offline Cryptographic Licensing Supporter Pass validation uses asymmetric NIST P-256 ECDSA public key verification. License keys are validated locally on the device without requiring persistent internet connections or central phone-home checkpoints. NIST P-256 ECDSA Data Minimisation & Ephemeral Handling Web contact forms, newsletter signups, and beta registrations collect strictly essential contact fields. Submissions are processed securely for correspondence and purged in accordance with our retention policy. UK GDPR Compliant Product-Specific Privacy Matrix Application / Service Data Storage & Scope Network & Cloud Transmission Dedicated Notice AmnShield Suite (Android / Windows / Extension) Local Room/SQLite DB, Preferences DataStore, custom keywords and blocklists. Zero network telemetry. Optional cloud sync via encrypted Supabase for Supporter Pass. AmnShield Privacy → AmniHaze Suite (Android / Extension) On-device LiteRT and TensorFlow Lite model weights. No image storage. 100% offline inference. Zero screen frames or captured camera pixels transmitted. AmniHaze Policy → Al-Haq Hub (Mobile & Web Platform) Local prayer calculation parameters, bookmarks, and UI preferences. Calculations computed on-device. No location histories or user identifiers tracked. Hub Policy → Quran Reader & Islamic Library Local reading position, audio reciter preferences, font sizing. Static content delivery. No personal reading history collected or monitored. Static Local-First Contact & Feedback Submissions Transient email address, sender name, and inquiry content. Processed over TLS directly to secure customer service inbox. Docs Hub → Your Rights (UK GDPR / DPA 2018) Under UK and European data protection legislation, you have the right to request access to, rectification of, or erasure of any personal data you have provided via our communications channels. Direct all privacy inquiries to: privacy@alhaq-initiative.org Data Controller Contact Controller: Habibur Rahman Meranai (trading as Al-Haq Studio & Al-Haq Initiative). Official Enquiries: contact@alhaq-initiative.org or legal@alhaq.uk. Responses are typically provided within 7 business days.

Tafsir & Commentary Ibn Kathir Tafsir One of the most comprehensive and respected tafsir works in Islamic scholarship. Al-Fatiha Tafsir "The Opening" - This surah is the foundation of the Quran and teaches us the proper way to address Allah in prayer. Al-Ikhlas Tafsir "The Sincerity" - This surah is equivalent to one-third of the Quran and emphasizes the pure monotheism of Islam. Ya-Sin Tafsir "The Heart of the Quran" - This surah addresses the truth of the Quran and the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Contemporary Tafsir Modern interpretations that address contemporary issues and challenges. Ma'ariful Quran A comprehensive modern tafir that explains the Quran in light of contemporary understanding. Tafsir Al-Tabari One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafir works, covering historical context and linguistic analysis. Tafsir Al-Qurtubi A detailed tafir that focuses on legal rulings and practical applications of Quranic verses. /quranhub.html.title: Quran Hub (Al-Haq Hub feature) - Al-Haq Initiative
/quranhub.html.content: Feature inside Al-Haq Hub · Beta Quran Hub AI-powered Quran recitation feedback and memorization practice. Quran Hub is now a feature inside the Al-Haq Hub mobile app (with an upcoming companion web app) — bringing real-time correction, moving highlight, and word-by-word analysis into the same daily-deen companion you already use for prayer times, Qibla, and adhkaar. Under the hood, Quran Hub is powered by our in-house AI engine, TaleemAI. Al-Haq Hub is the mobile app, Quran Hub is the feature inside it, and TaleemAI is the engine that makes the real-time recitation feedback possible. Real-time recitation correction and feedback — powered by TaleemAI Moving highlight and word-by-word analysis Multiple surahs and full-surah display Memorization practice with repetition and backward-correction recognition Ships inside Al-Haq Hub mobile (Android beta) · upcoming web app companion About Al-Haq Hub Join the Al-Haq Hub Beta Open the Quran reader (website) Note: this page describes the AI Quran Hub feature shipping inside Al-Haq Hub. The website's standalone Quran reader lives at /quran.html and is a separate web app. This free community tool is provided by the Al-Haq Initiative, developed by Al-Haq Studio (Al-Haq Digital Services & Solutions — UK sole trader).
